chapter_name: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
learning_objective: 🎯 Become a change-spotter and learn to tell the difference between simple shape-shifting changes and complete chemical transformations!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: When you tear a piece of paper or melt an ice cube, it looks different, but it is still paper and water! In a physical change, only the size, shape, or state changes. No brand new material is created, and you can often reverse it.

When you bake a cake or burn a log of wood, you cannot turn them back into raw batter or a wooden log. This is a chemical change! A completely new substance is formed, and these changes are mostly irreversible.

Have you seen old iron gates turning flaky and reddish-brown? When iron reacts with oxygen and moisture in the air, it forms a new substance called rust. This is a slow chemical change that eats away at the metal.

fun_activity.title: 🍞 The Bread Observation
fun_activity.instructions: Take a slice of bread. Tearing it into pieces is a physical change! Now, toast it in a toaster until it turns brown. Can you turn the toast back into soft white bread? No! Toasting is a chemical change.

quick_recap: ⭐ Physical changes alter the appearance or state but do not create new substances.
⭐ Chemical changes create entirely new substances and are usually permanent.
⭐ Rusting is a chemical change that happens when iron meets oxygen and water.
